10.1002_aenm.202503595: All‐solid‐state sodium batteries (ASSSBs) have attracted extensive attention for the high abundancy of sodium resources, enhanced safety, and superior energy density. As a critical component of ASSSBs, halide solid‐state electrolytes (SSEs) have been widely studied in recent years, but still suffer from low ion conductivity and poor interfacial contact with the cathode due to their high crystallinity. Here, a completely amorphized Na 1.33 Ta 0.67 Zr 0.33 Cl 6 (NTZC) SSEs is reported, with a remarkable ionic conductivity of 3.4 mS cm −1 at 25 °C and exceptional viscoelasticity. Zr‐doping induces complete amorphization via twisting the [TaCl 6 ] – octahedra. The distortion of the [TaCl 6 ] – octahedra not only enlarges Na + migration channels but also reduces the Cl − blocking effects on Na + transport, while Zr‐doping also expands the lattice volume due to its larger ionic radius compared to Ta 5+ . ASSSBs with the Na 0.95 Ni 0.33 Fe 0.33 Mn 0.33 O 2 cathode achieve 77.45% retention after 450 cycles at 0.5 C under high mass loading (20.85 mg cm −2 ). This work provides a feasible way for the design and preparation of sodium halide solid electrolytes in the future.
10.1002_smll.75967: A cooperative self‐assembly of organic small molecules made of diester/diacid‐bithiophene units [BT 2D ‐CE ( 1 ), BT 2D ‐CA ( 2 )] with hexylpyridine‐ or phosphonic acid‐functionalized dithienopyrrole units [DTP 2D ‐Py ( 3 ), DTP 2D ‐PA ( 4 )] was induced atop Nickel Oxide (NiO x ) hole‐transport‐layer for lead‐free tin‐based perovskite solar cells. The pyridine functionality of DTP 2D ‐Py ( 3 ) in conjunction with the carboxyl group of BT 2D ‐CA ( 2 ) altered the NiO x /Perovskite interfacial energetics and accelerates selective hole extraction by passivating the buried interfacial defects, resulting in a power conversion efficiency of 8.1% due to enhanced photovoltage (0.560 to 0.593 V), alongside remarkable operational stability. The crucial role of synergistic energy‐level modulation, especially the Fermi level, was unraveled using ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy, demonstrating that combining complementary conjugated organic backbones with targeted functionalities offers versatility for enhancement of overall device performance and stability.
10.1016_j.jenvman.2026.128968: Antibiotic contamination in aquatic environments poses a serious risk to public health and contributes to the emergence of antimicrobial resistance. In this study, a magnetic powder activated carbon derived from pulp and paper mill sludge, combined with Fe magnetic nanoparticles (PAC-Fe), was synthesized via a one-step activation and magnetization strategy for application in a flow mode heterogeneous solar photo-Fenton system. The PAC-Fe was applied for the degradation of sulfamethoxazole (SMX) and trimethoprim (TMP) in surface water at natural pH, under natural solar irradiation. The system achieved 91 % ± 2 % removal of SMX and complete removal of TMP, after 180 min of irradiation with the degradation kinetics fitted to the BMG model. The results indicate that the hydroxyl radical (HO•) drives the degradation pathway. In ultrapure water, TMP degradation occurred mainly in solution, while SMX transformation occurred primarily on the catalyst surface. In surface water, the participation of HO• was still evident, although the dominant reaction zone could not be distinguished. The PAC-Fe catalyst exhibited satisfactory magnetic properties, enabling easy post-treatment separation and potential reuse. Transformation products (TPs) were identified for both antibiotics, one for SMX and five for TMP, mostly resulting from hydroxylation and demethylation pathways. ECOSAR predictions indicated that several of the TPs showed increased chronic toxicity. Yet, the treatment led to complete elimination of antibacterial activity for all tested bacterial strains after degradation of SMX and TMP. These results confirm the viability of PAC-Fe-based solar photo-Fenton treatment for efficient removal of antibiotics at environmentally relevant concentrations in complex water matrices. • PAC-Fe was synthesized by one-step activation/magnetization. • PAC-Fe was applied in a flow mode heterogeneous solar photo-Fenton system. • Solar photo-Fenton removed 91 ± 2 % for SMX and 100% for TMP within 180 min at pH 8. • Hydroxyl radicals has a major role in degradation pathways. • Antibacterial activity was fully eliminated for 4 clinically relevant strains.
10.1016_j.tsep.2026.104903: The utilization of CO 2 -rich natural gas resources remains challenging due to the high energy penalty associated with conventional CO 2 separation processes and the relatively low methane content of the feed gas. In this study, chemical looping hydrogen (H 2 ) generation (CLHG) is proposed as an alternative pathway to directly convert CO 2 -rich raw natural gas (RNG) into H 2 while simultaneously achieving inherent carbon capture. The Natuna gas field, containing approximately 71.8% CO 2 and 26.4% CH 4 , was selected as a representative case of high CO 2 natural gas resources. Process simulation was conducted using Aspen Plus V14 with a Fe-based oxygen carrier in a three-reactor chemical looping configuration comprising a fuel reactor, a steam reactor, and an air reactor, integrated with gas turbines and an organic Rankine cycle for heat recovery. The thermodynamic analysis identified optimal operating conditions of 900 °C in the fuel reactor and 850 °C in the steam reactor. Under these conditions, the system achieves an H 2 efficiency of 42.2% with an H 2 yield of 0.02065 kg-H 2 /kg-RNG while generating 1017.44 kW/(kg-RNG/s). The process enables inherent CO 2 capture with a purity of 99.28%, exceeding typical post-combustion capture requirements. Energy analysis shows that approximately 2.9 MW of the 6.9 MW of RNG input is converted to H 2 , confirming that H 2 production is the dominant energy output of the system. The techno-economic assessment was performed by scaling the system to an industrial capacity of 5.56 kg-H 2 /s. At this scale, the plant is projected to generate 273.95 MW of net electricity. The resulting levelized cost of H 2 is estimated at 3.02 USD/kg-H 2 , which is lower than the current market price of blue H 2 . Sensitivity analysis further reveals that decreasing CO 2 content significantly enhances H 2 production and power generation while reducing the H 2 production cost. These results demonstrate that CLHG offers a promising utilization pathway for high-CO 2 natural gas resources, enabling simultaneous H 2 production and near-complete carbon capture while maintaining competitive H 2 production costs.
